title: Verbier and the 4 Vallées: Mont-Fort, Tortin and the Stairway to Heaven

bestPeriod.note: The Mont-Fort glacier holds snow all season; the Tortin face and lower Verbier slopes need a genuine cold spell to ski well, best from mid-January.

summary: A week in Verbier and the 4 Vallées built around Mont-Fort, the Stairway to Heaven and Tortin, with an honest read of where the lift interconnect actually breaks down.
hook: Verbier's reputation rests on one glacier cable car and the terrain it unlocks. The 4 Vallées network is genuinely vast, four linked valleys, over a hundred lifts between them, but almost everything this trip is built for depends on a single chain running from Verbier village to Mont-Fort at 3,330 m, and that chain has a well-known weak link at the top. This week is planned around it, not surprised by it.

snapshot.Best Period: January-March; mid-January onward for the Tortin face to be properly filled in
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: 4 Vallées network (Verbier, La Tzoumaz, Nendaz, Veysonnaz, Thyon, Siviez); base 820 m at Le Châble, top 3,330 m at Mont-Fort
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Geneva (GVA); shuttle or train via Martigny/Le Châble, roughly 2h to 2h30 total
snapshot.Who It Suits: Advanced and expert skiers and riders wanting guided glacier freeride and steep off-piste, comfortable in variable, ungroomed snow

itinerary.title: Arrival and gear check
itinerary.morning: Fly to Geneva; shuttle or train (Geneva-Martigny, then the Le Châble gondola) up to Verbier at 1,500 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Check into the base hotel and visit a rental shop for skis or a splitboard, boots and full avalanche kit, transceiver, probe, shovel. Register with La Fantastique or the Bureau des Guides de Verbier for the week's guided days.
itinerary.evening: Buy the 4 Vallées pass and check the Valais avalanche bulletin for the coming days.
itinerary.dayStats: 0 vertical metres skied · 0 sectors · 0 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Local orientation: Savoleyres and Lac des Vaux
itinerary.morning: Ride the Savoleyres gondola on Verbier's quieter, south-facing side, a good first day to read the group's ability on varied but non-glacial terrain.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Lac des Vaux and the lower Attelas sector, working toward the base of the Mont-Fort lift chain to see current conditions and queue length before committing a full day to it.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner; tomorrow starts early to beat the Mont-Fort queue.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,000 m vertical · 2 sectors (Savoleyres, Lac des Vaux) · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Mont-Fort and the Stairway to Heaven
itinerary.morning: Be at the Médran lift base in Verbier by 08:00. Ride up through Les Ruinettes to Attelas (2,727 m), then the Mont-Fort cable car to 3,330 m, the single access point to the glacier terrain and the most wind-sensitive lift in the network; it is the first thing to close in a storm and the reason this day is scheduled early in the week, not the last possible morning.
itinerary.afternoon: With a guide, ski the Stairway to Heaven: from the Mont-Fort glacier or Col des Gentianes, a long, roughly 2,000 m off-piste descent down the Combe de Tortin to the Tortin lift base. Crevasses on the upper glacier and variable snow on the lower combe make this a guided itinerary, run by La Fantastique or the Bureau des Guides de Verbier, not a solo line regardless of visible tracks.
itinerary.evening: Recovery dinner; this is the physically hardest day of the week.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,700 m vertical · 1 itinerary (Stairway to Heaven) · 3 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Tortin face and Siviez
itinerary.morning: Ride the Jumbo gondola from Le Châble/Verbier toward Attelas, then down into the Tortin sector via the Chassoure-Tortin cable car. The Tortin piste itself is one of the network's steepest marked runs, north-facing and mogul-prone by midday; ski it early while it is still firm rather than broken up.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue into Siviez and across toward Nendaz, sampling the interconnect's mid-mountain pistes, which are considerably gentler than the Verbier side.
itinerary.evening: Return via the same chain to Verbier.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,900 m vertical · 2 sectors (Tortin, Siviez/Nendaz) · 4.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: The full 4 Vallées traverse
itinerary.morning: A long point-to-point day linking Verbier through Siviez to Veysonnaz and on to Thyon, using the full chain of gondolas and chairlifts that gives the area its name. This is a logistics exercise as much as a ski day, plan lift closing times at each valley in advance, since missing the last connection strands you a taxi ride from Verbier.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the Thyon/Veysonnaz pistes, generally sunnier and lower-altitude than Mont-Fort, then begin the return traverse in good time.
itinerary.evening: Confirm the last uphill connection back over Attelas before it closes; if in doubt, descend to Le Châble by road transport rather than risk it.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,400 m vertical · 4 sectors (Verbier, Siviez, Veysonnaz, Thyon) · 5.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Second glacier day or La Tzoumaz bad-snow plan B
itinerary.morning: Check Mont-Fort's status before deciding: if it is running and the snowpack has stabilised, a second guided glacier itinerary off Col des Gentianes extends the week's off-piste tally. If the top chain is on wind hold or the lower slopes are worn thin by traffic and sun, switch to La Tzoumaz on the sunnier, more sheltered side of the valley, lower altitude but more forgiving and typically less crowded.
itinerary.afternoon: Either continuation of the glacier plan, or a relaxed tree-lined afternoon on La Tzoumaz's runs, a genuine fallback rather than a consolation prize.
itinerary.evening: Gear rinse and pack check ahead of the last day.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,200-2,700 m vertical · 1 sector (Mont-Fort or La Tzoumaz) · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Final morning and departure
itinerary.morning: A short session on the Savoleyres side, the most reliable sector for a low-key last morning regardless of what the top of the mountain is doing.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,300 m vertical · 1 sector (Savoleyres) · 2 lift hours.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Nevaï
accommodationStrategy.description: Close to the Médran lift base, the start point for the Mont-Fort chain, useful given how early Day 3 and any repeat glacier day need to start. Spa and sauna help with recovery after the Stairway to Heaven.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Verbier
accommodationStrategy.description: A straightforward central base within walking distance of Médran, Savoleyres and the village restaurants, without the design-hotel price premium.

accommodationStrategy.name: Chalet-style guesthouse, Le Châble
accommodationStrategy.description: A lower-cost option in the valley-floor town at the base of the Verbier gondola, useful for a longer stay or a group happy to add ten minutes to each lift-base commute.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; Switzerland's air rescue service Rega is 1414, the number to know for any serious off-piste incident.
logistics.weather: Check MeteoSwiss and the resort's own lift-status page each morning; Mont-Fort's status is the one figure that reshapes the whole day's plan.
logistics.bookingWindows: La Fantastique and the Bureau des Guides de Verbier fill February and Easter dates weeks ahead; book the Stairway to Heaven day as soon as your dates are fixed.
logistics.money: Switzerland uses the Swiss franc; cards are near-universal but small mountain restaurants sometimes prefer cash.
logistics.health: The Swiss avalanche bulletin (SLF) uses the same European 1-5 danger scale; carry transceiver, probe and shovel on every off-piste or glacier day, without exception.

other.label: Pass tiers, approx. 2026
other.text: A 4 Vallées adult one-day pass runs approx. CHF 94 (approx. €99); a six-day pass approx. CHF 409 (approx. €430). Buying online at least ten days ahead typically carries a discount over walk-up prices, book the week in advance rather than at the lift base.

other.label: Verbier is not on the Magic Pass
other.text: Switzerland's popular multi-resort Magic Pass covers roughly forty smaller and mid-sized areas, but Verbier/4 Vallées, like most premium big-name resorts, sells its own standalone pass, do not assume cross-honour with a Magic Pass bought elsewhere in Switzerland.

other.label: Where the interconnect breaks down
other.text: The entire glacier side of the network funnels through the Attelas-Mont-Fort cable car chain; this is the most wind-exposed lift in the system and the first to close in poor weather, at which point Tortin, Siviez and the glacier terrain all become unreachable from Verbier until it reopens.

proTips: Ski Mont-Fort and the Stairway to Heaven early in the week, not the last possible day, it is the lift most likely to be closed by wind, and a mid-week backup day only works if you have not saved everything for Day 7.
Ride the first cabin up Médran; the queue for Attelas and Mont-Fort builds fast after 09:00 in high season.
Ski Tortin before midday, its steep, mogulled face is far more manageable firm than it is broken up by an afternoon of traffic.
Buy the 4 Vallées pass online at least ten days ahead for the standard advance discount rather than at the lift-base ticket office.
On the full-traverse day, write down each connecting lift's last-departure time before setting out, the return chain over Attelas closes earlier than the village lifts.
If Mont-Fort is closed, do not wait it out at the base, La Tzoumaz's sheltered side is often skiing perfectly well while the glacier chain sits idle.

packingNotes: Full avalanche kit: transceiver, probe, shovel, non-negotiable for the Stairway to Heaven and any other off-piste day.
Wide, freeride-oriented skis or a freeride splitboard; the marked pistes here are a minority of what this trip actually skis.
A hardshell and a genuinely warm midlayer, Mont-Fort at 3,330 m runs 15-20°C colder than the village and is routinely windy.
Glacier glasses or category 4 goggle lenses for the high glacier terrain.
A small pack for skins, water and a spare layer on the full-traverse day.
Comfortable off-mountain shoes for Verbier's steep village streets, which see plenty of foot traffic between hotel and lift.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Mont-Fort is closed by wind.** Fallback: switch immediately to La Tzoumaz or the Tortin/Siviez sector if already accessible, and hold a spare mid-week day to retry the glacier chain.
**Tortin is icy or bare after a dry, cold spell.** Fallback: this face needs real snow depth; default to Savoleyres or the Nendaz side, which hold artificial and natural cover better.

**The full-traverse day runs long and a connection is missed.** Fallback: descend to the nearest valley-floor town (Nendaz, Veysonnaz or Thyon all have road transport) and return to Verbier by taxi or bus rather than pushing a closing lift.

**Guided departures are fully booked.** Fallback: book La Fantastique or the Bureau des Guides de Verbier before arrival, not on Day 1, this is the single most common reason groups miss the Stairway to Heaven.

**A storm cycle closes the upper mountain for several days.** Fallback: Savoleyres and the lower Verbier pistes, more sheltered and tree-lined, keep the week skiable while waiting the glacier terrain out.
